trimmingSuggestions.description: The animated scenes (3 and part of 4) and the scene with Dave in the temple explaining the rules (scene 5) could be shortened to maintain a more consistent pace and focus on Dave's personal experience at the meditation camp. The explanation of the daily routine (scene 7) could also be more concise. The Backstreet Boys fast cuts in scene 5 can be removed as they are not contributing to the narrative. The initial scenes 0, 1, and 2 could also be shortened or made more dynamic to immediately capture the viewer's attention.

Well, it's because of all the things you read, the funny catch you see in your feet, advertisements
on the street, the chat lady asking if there's anything you need, the message from your
friend that wants to meet, multitask and watch TV while you eat, notification of a new
twig, something on the news about corporate greed or that's shown with a sick beat.
In the techno world, data is what we eat. We progress a zillion things on high speed. Our
brain takes care of all this mess, it can make you feel happy, sick or even depressed.
It's powerful and controls the way how we feel, but we don't put a lot of effort in keeping
it real fit. I mean, we train our body, work out, get a massage and drink a carriage
juice organic grown, but our mind is left on its own. It's time to be kind and train
the mind.
Hello, so I'm currently in Thailand, in Chiang Mai, a city in the north, and I'm on my
way to a Buddhist temple where I'm gonna spend 10 days living with the monks to train
the mind. I think we're pretty close, it sounds like we're pretty close. Should be a
fierce.
It is very peaceful here with a lot of beautiful temples. The amount of work I put in these
things is amazing. Check out these old beautiful food cars.
And obviously, a lot of monks, interesting to see what they do in daily life. Here they
all practice the fipa sana meditation. It's where you learn to control your mind. It's
like a camp where they improve your concentration. Like a big concentration camp. No, that sounds
a bit off. Let's color the meditation camp. I'll be staying here for the coming 10 days
to make my mind stronger. That's my room. My room for the coming days, it looks comfortable.
But, in order to hang out with the monks, you need a few things. A couple of these smelly
sticks, 11 white flowers, some orange yellow candles, and you need to wear white clothing.
It makes me look like a backstreet boy. Besides getting these stains, there's also a few
rules. Don't read, so not even books about Buddhism or meditation. You don't write either,
so don't write down your thoughts. You don't talk. Now, they actually wrote this in here.
It's pretty simple, but not talking. I don't think I ever done that for 10 days. Oh,
and finally, you can't listen to music. No internet, wifi, phones, or cameras. So I'm
going to leave you here and see you back in 10 days.
Oh, feels good to talk to him. So I just finished, and that has to be one of the most boring
things I've done in my entire life. Let me get some explain why.
First off, the haircut. No need to do this, but they say it's easier for your thoughts
to leave the mind. I figured, let's try it out. So let me explain the daily routine first.
So this is one day here, and they're pretty much all the same. It starts at 4am and you
go meditating right out of bed. 6.30, breakfast, usually a noodle soup. You go back meditating,
they have lunch. This is also the last meal of the day. In the afternoon, you clean yourself,
the room, and you pick up some leaves from the ground, because...
A clean environment helps to get a clean mind.
When you do some more meditation, and at 5, there's a cup of choosed soup.
And all this time in between, you do meditation. At 10 o'clock, you go to bed and sleep for
about 6 hours.
So as you can see, there isn't much to do in one day except a lot of meditation. This
is quite boring, because meditation itself is not necessarily exciting. The time goes
by super slow and you're just sitting there in the room. However, here is what's nice about it.
Let's say a disline you're chill, and this line means chaos. Usually, there are a lot of things
on your mind in a day, a monkey mind. And then you go into meditation, where there is nothing going
on, really nothing, it's super boring. But slowly, you notice your brain starts to mellow down,
and at this point, there are still some old thoughts going through your mind, but you learn
to control these. And since there's no new input at all, you start to become more chill.
And this really feels like your brain is one big chaos of thoughts, which are slowly cleaned up
and going away. Which gives you a much cleaner mind. And this is when I realized how long it's
been that I had an empty mind. There's always something to worry, think, or wonder about.
But that feeling of having an empty mind and living in the present, it's pretty nice.
It's like being a kid again, and you finish your homework, and nothing else on your mind.
